title: Usage
text:
integrate(ex, x)                 # indefinite integral
integrate(ex, x, y, …)           # iterated: ∫ … (∫ ex dx) dy …
integrate(ex, (x, a, b), …)      # definite: F(b) - F(a) The answer is a term of the same package as ex (without a constant of integration), or an IntegralWithRootSums …

title: SymbolicUtils.jl
text:
SymbolicUtils terms implement the TermInterface methods and are integrated directly. Constants such as sqrt(2) are kept exact (they are built with TermInterface.maketerm; SymbolicUtils would otherwise evaluate sqrt(2) to a floating point number): using SymbolicUtils: @syms
using RischIntegrate: …

text:
Symbolics wraps its SymbolicUtils terms in Num, which does not implement the TermInterface methods: unwrap the integrand and the variable, and wrap the answer again. using Symbolics

title: Giac.jl
text:
Giac terms implement the TermInterface methods (through Giac's TermInterface extension) and are integrated directly; Giac's ln is read as log: using Giac
using RischIntegrate: integrate
@giac_var x

integrate(log(x)^2, x)      # 2*x-2*x*ln(x)+x*ln(x)^2
integrate(1 / (x^2 + 2), x) # …

title: Expr and other term types
text: The keywords build and lift say how the answer is built: build(op, args...) makes the term for the function op (+, *, sqrt, log, …) applied to the terms args, and lift(n) turns a Julia number into a term. By default operations are called as functions. For Expr: using RischIntegrate: …

title: Non-elementary integrals
text: Integrals that can be written with the special functions of SpecialFunctions.jl (expinti, sinint, cosint, erf, erfi) and PolyLog.jl (li2) are returned that way, when the term type has methods for them (SymbolicUtils does): integrate(exp(-x^2), …

title: RootSums
text: When the residues of the logarithmic part are algebraic of degree greater than 2, the answer is an IntegralWithRootSums: an elementary term plus sums over the roots of a polynomial. It can be evaluated numerically; the logarithms are continued along the real line, so F(b) - F(a) is a definite …

title: How it works
text: The integrand is parsed into an exact differential field and integrated there by the Risch algorithm, following Bronstein, Symbolic Integration I. The answer is checked by differentiation in the same field, then rebuilt as a term of the user's package.

title: The steps
text: Rational functions : Hermite reduction (Bronstein §2.2) gives the rational part, the Rothstein–Trager resultant the logarithmic part. Quadratic residues give log and atan terms over  (with Rioboo's LogToAtan for real, continuous atan terms); quartic residues are written with real radicals when …

text: RootSum Σ_{Q(α)=0} α log W(α, x): poly is Q(z) (monic, squarefree; coefficients low → high) and W the coefficients of W(z, x) in x (low → high), each a polynomial in z reduced mod Q. var is how the variable prints and arg the term it stands for (after a substitution such as t = sqrt(1 + x) …

title: RischIntegrate.TermRootSum
text: TermRootSum Σ_{Q(α)=0} α log W(α) with W(α) = Σ_j coeffs[j] α^(j-1), the coeffs being terms of the user's package (a RootSum found inside a tower, e.g. in log(x)). rs(a) evaluates numerically at x = a.

title: RischIntegrate.NotElementary
text: NotElementary The integral was proved to have no elementary antiderivative (and no form with the special functions used by the package was found).

title: RischIntegrate.RischNotImplemented
text: RischNotImplemented The integrand lies outside the cases implemented: no answer, and no decision whether the integral is elementary.

title: RischIntegrate.RischError
text: RischError An internal error, e.g. an answer that failed its own check by differentiation. It indicates a bug.

title: RischIntegrate.jl
